Reviewed the diff, the bot comments (Codex: no findings; CodeRabbit: no actionable comments, just a docstring-coverage nit I'd disregard here), and the existing `StreamExtensions`/`PlaidItemsController` code this builds on.

A few observations beyond what's already been flagged:

- The new `frame_redirect_to` generalizes a pattern that already exists verbatim in `PlaidItemsController#render_frame_redirect`, `BinanceItemsController`, and `CoinbaseItemsController` (same `render html: helpers.turbo_frame_tag(turbo_frame_request_id) { helpers.turbo_stream.action(:redirect, path) }` body). Those three call sites gate on `turbo_frame_request?` themselves before calling the private helper, whereas the new shared method folds that check in and falls back to a normal `redirect_to`. That's a sound generalization and matches the stated goal of not adding a ninth copy — worth a follow-up issue to migrate those three existing call sites onto `frame_redirect_to` too, since now there are two near-identical implementations of the same trick living side by side in the codebase.
- Logic in each of the 9 controllers is a pure one-line swap (`redirect_to` → `frame_redirect_to`) with no change to the tenancy/lookup logic (`Current.family.*`, `requested_*_item`, etc.), so no new authorization or tenancy surface here.
- The `wise_items_controller.rb` change correctly preserves the `and return` idiom, and `frame_redirect_to` returns a truthy value on both branches (`redirect_to`/`render`), so that still short-circuits as intended.
- Test coverage looks adequate and consistent with existing conventions in this controller family (Mocha stubs / `scheduled_for_deletion` fixtures to force the "not configured" branch, `Turbo-Frame: modal` header, asserting the `turbo-stream[action=redirect]` target, and the flash alert). Wise's non-frame test is a nice touch others didn't add.
- Nothing API/UI-DS-relevant here (no ERB/CSS/API controller changes), so those checklist items don't apply.

No blocking issues found; this is consistent with the established pattern and conventions.
